recognize_zh: 毛囊漏斗部管腔內有一隻細長、外有薄殼、內含顆粒狀物質的節肢動物體，位置緊鄰下方皮脂腺，形態符合毛囊蟲（Demodex folliculorum）；周圍毛囊上皮與真皮無明顯發炎。
features: Elongated, cigar-shaped mite within a dilated follicular infundibulum
Thin refractile chitinous exoskeleton enclosing granular internal contents
Surrounding stratified follicular epithelium is intact with no significant inflammatory infiltrate
Adjacent sebaceous lobules with clear vacuolated sebocytes
Black pigment fragment within the follicular lumen, likely extraneous material
describe_en: Scalp skin biopsy shows a hair follicle with an adjacent sebaceous gland. Within the dilated follicular infundibulum there is an elongated mite with a thin refractile exoskeleton and granular internal contents, consistent with Demodex folliculorum. The follicular epithelium is intact and there is no significant perifollicular inflammation, granuloma formation, or follicular rupture in this field. An extraneous black pigment fragment is noted in the lumen. Findings are consistent with incidental Demodex folliculorum infestation of the hair follicle.

ddx.vs: D. brevis is shorter and resides within sebaceous and meibomian glands rather than the follicular lumen.
Scabies mites are round, lie in burrows within the stratum corneum, and are not intrafollicular.
Pathogenic demodicosis shows multiple mites per follicle with perifollicular lymphohistiocytic or granulomatous inflammation, absent in this field.
